F18.quote: We are also releasing a new research primer, "Myths about Generative AI, Productivity, and Labor Displacement", which discusses five common myths around generative AI at work. This primer will be the first of many.
F18.claim: Alex Hanna, quoted on the page: a primer on five common myths about generative AI at work, 'the first of many' (her title has 'Labor Displacement')
F18.lineage: the primer: myths about generative AI, productivity and job displacement

F19.quote: In our primer, we discuss how "AI" is a cudgel against workers and a set of technologies premised on labor intensification. They don't increase productivity and break work processes and norms.
F19.claim: Alex Hanna, quoted on the page: the primer treats 'AI' as a cudgel against workers and technologies premised on labor intensification, which do not increase productivity
F19.lineage: the primer's argument: displacement as a firm's market strategy

F20.quote: The hub's core argument, as stated on its project page, is that workers are being displaced by AI "not due to the actual ability of AI technology doing the jobs of workers to the same quality, or even to a sufficient quality." Instead, the lab characterizes it as "a market-oriented move by firms to brag about becoming AI-first, while finding cost-savings by laying off employees."
F20.claim: AI Weekly, quoting the hub: workers are displaced not because AI does their jobs to the same or a sufficient quality, but by 'a market-oriented move by firms to brag about becoming AI-first, while finding cost-savings by laying off employees'
F20.lineage: the primer's argument: displacement as a firm's market strategy

F21.quote: That reframing shifts the conversation from technological inevitability to strategic choice, giving organizers different ground to stand on in collective bargaining.
F21.claim: AI Weekly's own reading: the reframing moves the conversation from technological inevitability to strategic choice, and gives organizers ground in collective bargaining
F21.lineage: the primer's argument: displacement as a firm's market strategy

F22.locus: ¶ 'One thing to keep in mind' s1–2
F22.quote: One thing to keep in mind is that this is advocacy-oriented research. The primer's specific arguments are not retrievable from the public page without downloading the documents, so it is not possible to assess whether the "myths" framing holds up against the broader empirical literature on AI productivity.
F22.claim: AI Weekly's limit: advocacy-oriented research, whose 'myths' framing it could not assess against the empirical literature on AI productivity

F23.quote: The Luddite Lab's framing matters for practitioners on both sides of the bargaining table: if displacement is primarily a cost-cutting strategy rather than a genuine capability story, it changes what evidence is relevant in AI-related labor disputes. The primer format, available in both executive summary and full versions, is designed for practical use by organizers, not just academics. Watch whether this specific 'myths' framing starts appearing in collective bargaining proposals in journalism, entertainment, and nursing.
F23.claim: AI Weekly's editor's note: the framing bears on what evidence counts in AI-related labor disputes; the primer is made for organizers; whether it appears in collective bargaining proposals is a thing to watch
